nodes.label: Dimension 1: Strategy, Leadership & Value Realization
nodes.summary: Assessment dimension 1 of the nine-dimension maturity model: Strategy, Leadership & Value Realization. Contains 8 criteria scored L1-L5.

nodes.label: 1.1 AI & Agentic Vision / Ambition (fit autonomy, augmentation-first)
aliases: AI & Agentic Vision / Ambition (fit autonomy, augmentation-first)
nodes.summary: Sets the altitude. In 2026, maturity = matching autonomy to value/risk and maximizing augmentation, NOT maximizing autonomy.

anchors.L1: No vision; AI talked about, not directed
anchors.L2: Vision = 'become autonomous'; autonomy treated as the goal
anchors.L3: Written end-state; autonomy considered per use case
anchors.L4: Augmentation-first operating model; autonomy matched to value/risk; socialized
anchors.L5: Deliberate human-AI operating model; augmentation maximized, autonomy only where value>cost; adapts as tech shifts

probing_questions.q: What does the enterprise look like in 3 years if AI/agents succeed?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether a concrete end-state exists. Strong: a vivid, specific picture of what's different and how people work with AI. Weak: vague 'more efficient' or silence → vision absent.

probing_questions.q: Is more autonomy the goal, or do you match autonomy to the value and the cost-of-being-wrong of each use case?
probing_questions.looking_for: The core 2026 test. Strong: autonomy is fitted per use case by value/risk; not an end in itself. Weak: 'become a fully autonomous enterprise' as the goal → chasing the low-yield pattern that mostly fails.

probing_questions.q: Where is your value coming from — augmenting people via reusable skills, or autonomous end-to-end agents?
probing_questions.looking_for: Augmentation is the higher-value zone today. Strong: augmentation-first, autonomy applied selectively where justified. Weak: the program is bet on autonomous agents → high failure risk, lower realized value.

probing_questions.q: Has leadership written down and socialized an AI/agent vision?
probing_questions.looking_for: Separates a shared vision from hallway talk. Strong: documented, communicated, referenced in decisions. Weak: lives in a few heads → won't align the org.

nodes.label: 1.2 Business-AI Strategic Alignment
nodes.summary: Start from business needs; the build-vs-need gap drives 70-80% of scale failures.

anchors.L1: Tech-led; no link to business goals
anchors.L2: Some initiatives loosely tied to goals
anchors.L3: Each priority initiative traces to an objective; business owns it
anchors.L4: Eng-AI & business-AI run as one operating model
anchors.L5: Alignment continuous; portfolio re-shaped by strategy

probing_questions.q: Which business goals does each major AI initiative serve?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests outcome-orientation vs. tech-for-its-own-sake. Strong: each maps to a named business goal. Weak: tech-led experiments → scale-failure risk.

probing_questions.q: Can you trace each initiative to a specific strategic objective?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes portfolio traceability. Strong: explicit linkage maintained. Weak: can't trace → misalignment, wasted spend.

probing_questions.q: Who from the business (not IT) owns each initiative's outcome?
probing_questions.looking_for: Reveals whether the business owns value or it's an IT science project. Strong: a named business owner accountable for results. Weak: only IT owns → adoption/value gap.

probing_questions.q: Are engineering-AI and business-AI governed as one operating model?
probing_questions.looking_for: 2026 convergence test. Strong: unified governance/operating model. Weak: separate budgets/teams → duplication and fragmentation.

nodes.label: 1.3 Executive Sponsorship & Accountability
nodes.summary: Strongest predictor: exec alignment cuts failure ~67%; ~65% blame weak sponsorship.

anchors.L3: Named accountable sponsor per program
anchors.L4: Active C-suite forum clears blockers enterprise-wide
anchors.L5: AI value is a standing board-level accountability

probing_questions.q: Who is personally accountable for AI value at the executive level?
probing_questions.looking_for: Identifies single-point accountability (the strongest success predictor). Strong: a named C-level owner. Weak: a committee or nobody → stalls at first obstacle.

probing_questions.q: How regularly does the sponsor engage (decision forums, demos)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Distinguishes active from nominal sponsorship. Strong: regular cadence making real decisions. Weak: rare/ceremonial → not real backing.

probing_questions.q: Does leadership actively clear blockers and reallocate resources?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether sponsorship has teeth. Strong: concrete examples of cleared blockers/reallocation. Weak: passive support → initiatives starve.

probing_questions.q: Is sponsorship per-project or enterprise-wide?
probing_questions.looking_for: Reveals whether AI is strategic or a set of pet projects. Strong: an enterprise mandate. Weak: project-by-project → no scale.

nodes.label: 1.4 Prioritization, Portfolio Focus & Value Discernment
nodes.summary: The bottleneck is choosing; and in 2026 you must screen out 'agent-washed' RPA dressed up as multi-agent.

anchors.L3: Documented scoring; capability assessed beyond labels
anchors.L4: Portfolio managed; resourcing matched to real value, not labels
anchors.L5: Dynamic value-based portfolio; disciplined kill/scale; immune to agent-washing

probing_questions.q: How do you decide which use cases to fund?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests for a deliberate selection method vs. enthusiasm. Strong: explicit criteria (value/feasibility/data/cost-of-wrong). Weak: loudest voice wins → scattered bets.

probing_questions.q: When vendors pitch 'multi-agent systems', do you assess actual autonomy, capability and value — or accept the label?
probing_questions.looking_for: Anti-'agent-washing' test. Strong: due diligence on real capability/value; rejects relabeled RPA. Weak: buys the label → pays agent prices for workflow automation.

probing_questions.q: How many initiatives are active vs. resourced to actually succeed?
probing_questions.looking_for: Surfaces over-spread, the default failure mode. Strong: few, well-resourced bets. Weak: many shallow pilots → none reach escape velocity.

probing_questions.q: What have you explicitly chosen NOT to do?
probing_questions.looking_for: Strategy is choice; saying no is the tell. Strong: clear de-scoping decisions. Weak: 'everything' → no real prioritization.

nodes.label: 1.5 Investment & Funding Model
nodes.summary: At scale, poor unit economics can erase the margin AI was meant to defend; error-recovery cost is part of true TCO (ties to Dim 6.2).

anchors.L1: No dedicated funding / one-off; recovery cost ignored
anchors.L2: Pilots funded ad-hoc, no business case
anchors.L3: Funding gated by business case for priority work
anchors.L4: Funding intent + run-cost/unit economics modelled, incl. error-recovery cost
anchors.L5: Capital allocated dynamically by proven return; full TCO (build+run+recovery) feeds go/no-go

probing_questions.q: How are AI initiatives funded (innovation pot, BU budgets, central)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Reveals whether funding is intentional and sustainable. Strong: a clear, fit-for-purpose model. Weak: ad-hoc scraps → pilots starve.

probing_questions.q: Is a business case required to fund — and to continue funding?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests funding discipline and stage-gating. Strong: business case to start and to continue. Weak: fund-and-forget → zombie projects.

probing_questions.q: Do you model run-cost / unit (inference) economics before scaling?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes scale-economics awareness (margin risk). Strong: unit economics modeled pre-scale. Weak: unaware → cost blowouts at scale.

probing_questions.q: Who owns the inference / token bill?
probing_questions.looking_for: Reveals cost accountability. Strong: a clear owner watching spend. Weak: nobody → runaway cost.

probing_questions.q: Does the TCO include the cost of ERROR RECOVERY — the expected cost of detecting, correcting, and reversing agent mistakes (rework, remediation, downstream impact), not just inference and build?
probing_questions.looking_for: 2026 honesty check, ties to Dim 6.2 reversibility. Strong: recovery cost is modeled in TCO and feeds the go/no-go gate. Weak: only build+inference counted → TCO understated, autonomy looks cheaper than it is.

nodes.label: 1.6 Value Definition & Benefits Realization
nodes.summary: Only ~29% of execs measure ROI confidently; capability/vanity-defined success is a failure tell; augmentation value is often the real win.

anchors.L2: ROI claimed via vanity metrics (agents deployed)
anchors.L3: Business-delta KPIs + baselines for priority use cases
anchors.L4: Augmentation + automation value tracked, realized-vs-forecast, scale/kill decisions made
anchors.L5: Value-driver trees + stage-gates run the portfolio; augmentation value fully counted

probing_questions.q: Is success defined as a capability or a business delta?
probing_questions.looking_for: The classic failure tell. Strong: business deltas ('cut returns by N pts by Q3'). Weak: capability claims ('the model can predict X') → can't prove value.

probing_questions.q: Do you count augmentation / productivity value, or only autonomous end-to-end automation?
probing_questions.looking_for: 2026 rebasing: most value is augmentation. Strong: augmentation/productivity gains are measured and valued. Weak: only 'full automation' counts → undervalues the real win, over-pursues autonomy.

probing_questions.q: Do you report vanity metrics (number of agents/copilots deployed) or business outcomes?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests for substance vs. theatre. Strong: business outcomes. Weak: 'we deployed N agents' → activity mistaken for value.

probing_questions.q: Do you track realized vs. forecast benefits, and have you scaled or killed based on it?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether measurement drives decisions. Strong: cadence + concrete scale/kill examples. Weak: forecast-only, nothing killed → measurement isn't real.

nodes.label: 1.7 Sourcing & Stack Strategy (2026)
nodes.summary: Build-vs-buy is now a placement decision; standardizing is where scaling leverage lives — and where you avoid paying agent prices for relabeled RPA.

anchors.L1: Every team improvises; buys on labels
anchors.L3: Documented build/buy/managed rule; capability assessed beyond labels
anchors.L4: Standard harness + managed/self-host policy; MCP/A2A stance
anchors.L5: Deliberate, vendor-agnostic stack; advantage parked in the knowledge layer

probing_questions.q: Have you standardized a harness/runtime, or does each team build its own?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests for an operating-model standard vs. fragmentation. Strong: a chosen standard with rationale. Weak: every team improvises → sprawl, rework.

probing_questions.q: Can you distinguish genuine agentic capability from relabeled RPA/workflow when you buy or build?
probing_questions.looking_for: Anti-'agent-washing' discernment at sourcing. Strong: buys capability, not a label; knows what's under the hood. Weak: accepts vendor framing → overpays for workflow automation.

probing_questions.q: Managed vs. self-hosted, and what is your interoperability stance (MCP / A2A)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes deliberate placement and lock-in awareness. Strong: a clear rule by sensitivity/scale + standards posture. Weak: no view → accidental architecture and lock-in.

probing_questions.q: Is there a build-vs-buy-vs-managed decision rule?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests for repeatable sourcing discipline. Strong: a documented rule applied consistently. Weak: case-by-case improvisation.

nodes.label: 1.8 Adaptability & Pattern Resilience (build-to-delete)
nodes.summary: AI patterns churn yearly (chatbot->agentic->harness/skills); over-committing to a pattern/vendor creates write-offs.

anchors.L1: Big bets on one pattern/vendor; unaware of churn
anchors.L2: Aware patterns change, no deliberate response
anchors.L3: Some durable-asset focus; lock-in acknowledged
anchors.L4: Build-to-delete posture; durable assets prioritized; model/harness swappable
anchors.L5: Strategy assumes churn; advantage parked in durable assets (skills/data); re-platforms cheaply

probing_questions.q: If the dominant agent pattern shifts again in 12 months, what would you have to throw away?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests exposure to pattern churn. Strong: little is wasted — durable assets survive. Weak: large bespoke builds would be written off → fragile strategy.

probing_questions.q: Are you investing in durable assets (skills, data, knowledge) or in brittle orchestration / bespoke loops?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes where the bet is parked. Strong: durable assets that outlast patterns. Weak: heavy investment in brittle plumbing that the next model release breaks.

probing_questions.q: How locked-in are you to a specific vendor or pattern, and can you swap models/harnesses cheaply?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests lock-in and build-to-delete posture. Strong: swappable, vendor-agnostic. Weak: deeply coupled → can't adapt when the field moves.

probing_questions.q: Does leadership treat fast pattern change as a planning assumption?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests strategic realism. Strong: churn is assumed and planned for. Weak: treats today's pattern as permanent → over-commits.

nodes.label: Dimension 2: Knowledge Building & Capability Reuse
nodes.summary: Assessment dimension 2 of the nine-dimension maturity model: Knowledge Building & Capability Reuse. Contains 7 criteria scored L1-L5.

nodes.label: 2.1 Knowledge Capture & Codification
nodes.summary: Uncodified tacit knowledge is invisible to agents; codified expertise is the moat.

anchors.L1: Knowledge in heads (all functions); not mapped
anchors.L3: Sources mapped; expert procedures across functions codified into skills for priority areas
anchors.L4: Systematic codification pipeline; tacit knowledge routinely externalized
anchors.L5: Continuous capture; codified expertise is a managed, expanding moat

probing_questions.q: Where does your most valuable expertise live across functions (PM, ops, projects, eng, analysts) — and have you mapped it?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether the org knows where its tacit knowledge sits — the prerequisite to codifying it. Strong: a deliberate map of critical expertise and who holds it. Weak: 'in people's heads', unmapped → can't codify, key-person risk.

probing_questions.q: Are experts' procedures/judgment being codified into skills, or only documented?
probing_questions.looking_for: Distinguishes executable skills from passive docs. Strong: know-how turned into runnable skills. Weak: wikis/SOPs only → not usable by agents.

probing_questions.q: How do you codify know-how without flattening its nuance?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes whether judgment, edge cases and the 'why' survive — not just happy-path steps. Strong: experts review; edge cases + rationale captured; tested on hard cases; feedback loop. Weak: thin checklists → confidently wrong output.

probing_questions.q: What stops a senior expert's knowledge from leaving with them?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests resilience to attrition (key-person risk). Strong: critical expertise codified and shared. Weak: knowledge walks out the door when they leave.

nodes.label: 2.2 Skill / Capability Packaging (Assetization)
nodes.summary: Build once, reuse anywhere (any function); else the 2nd time you do similar work costs as much as the 1st.

anchors.L1: Repeatable work redone ad-hoc each time
anchors.L3: Skills packaged as versioned modular assets with a spec
anchors.L4: Composable library; new work assembled largely from existing skills
anchors.L5: Assetization is the default; cross-harness, cross-function portable skills

probing_questions.q: Are repeatable workflows (any function) captured as versioned, executable skills — or ad-hoc prompts/docs/tribal knowledge?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests assetization across the org. Strong: versioned, executable skills. Weak: scattered prompts/tribal practice → no leverage.

probing_questions.q: Are capabilities built as modular, reusable components?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes composability. Strong: modular building blocks that recombine. Weak: monolithic one-offs.

probing_questions.q: When you do similar work a second time (another QBR, vendor review, postmortem, service, or agent), how much is an existing reusable skill vs. redone by hand?
probing_questions.looking_for: The reuse-vs-rebuild test; reveals whether cost compounds or stays linear. Strong: most is reused, only the genuinely new part is built. Weak: rebuilt each time → no compounding, work costs full price every time.

probing_questions.q: Is there a standard format/spec for a 'skill' that any function can publish to?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests for a common contract enabling org-wide reuse. Strong: a shared spec/format. Weak: none → incompatible, un-shareable assets.

nodes.label: 2.3 Reuse Registry / Marketplace & Discovery
nodes.summary: Reuse only happens if people can find and attach what exists in seconds.

anchors.L1: No catalog; teams unaware of each other
anchors.L3: Central registry; indexed by owner/version/capability
anchors.L4: Discovery in seconds; reuse across functions/teams/geos; portable
anchors.L5: Internal marketplace; cross-harness discovery; self-service reuse

probing_questions.q: Is there a central catalog where skills/agents are discoverable?
probing_questions.looking_for: Discovery is the precondition for reuse. Strong: a real registry/catalog. Weak: none → siloed rebuilds.

probing_questions.q: Are assets indexed by owner, version, and capability?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests catalog quality/governance metadata. Strong: indexed and searchable. Weak: a dumping ground → effectively unusable.

probing_questions.q: Can a team find and reuse an existing skill in minutes, or do they rebuild?
probing_questions.looking_for: The practical discovery test. Strong: fast self-service find + attach. Weak: can't find it → rebuild.

probing_questions.q: Are skills portable across harnesses/teams?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes cross-harness/cross-team portability (2026). Strong: portable. Weak: locked to one team or tool.

nodes.label: 2.4 Reuse Governance, Quality & Security
nodes.summary: Skills are the new packages: reuse without governance scales risk as fast as value.

anchors.L3: Ownership, versioning, certification for priority skills
anchors.L4: CoE standards; third-party skills security-vetted; deprecation process
anchors.L5: Automated quality/security gates; trusted supply chain; continuous assurance

probing_questions.q: Who certifies a skill as safe and fit for reuse?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the trust/quality gate that makes reuse safe. Strong: a clear certification owner/process. Weak: anything runs → no trust, reuse stalls.

probing_questions.q: Is there versioning, ownership, and a deprecation process?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests lifecycle hygiene. Strong: owned, versioned, deprecated cleanly. Weak: stale/duplicated skills accumulate.

probing_questions.q: How do you vet external/third-party skills for security?
probing_questions.looking_for: Skills are packages → supply-chain risk (280k+ public skills, documented malicious ones). Strong: security vetting of third-party skills. Weak: unvetted → unsafe skills in production.

probing_questions.q: Are reusability and quality standards defined (e.g., by a CoE)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether standards exist to keep reuse safe and consistent. Strong: CoE standards. Weak: none → inconsistent quality.

nodes.label: 2.5 Trajectory Capture & Learning Flywheel
nodes.summary: Closed-loop feedback is the compounding mechanism that widens the gap over rivals.

anchors.L3: Trajectories captured for key skills/agents
anchors.L4: Closed-loop improvement on priority skills; corrections stored with assets
anchors.L5: Systematic flywheel; every interaction improves the library; trajectories a managed moat

probing_questions.q: Do you capture agent/skill execution trajectories (successes and failures)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Trajectories are the improvement dataset ('the harness is the dataset'). Strong: captured systematically. Weak: not captured → no basis to learn.

probing_questions.q: Does each use of a skill/agent feed back to improve it?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the closed loop that makes assets compound. Strong: usage improves the asset. Weak: static assets → they decay.

probing_questions.q: Are corrections stored with the skill/data for the next iteration?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes whether learning is retained. Strong: corrections persisted with the asset. Weak: lessons lost → same failures recur.

probing_questions.q: Who owns the improvement loop?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests accountability for continuous improvement. Strong: a named owner. Weak: nobody → the flywheel never turns.

nodes.label: 2.6 Measurement of Reuse & Value
nodes.summary: What gets measured gets funded; unmeasured reuse stays incidental.

anchors.L3: Reuse rate tracked for core assets
anchors.L4: Time-to-build reduction + reuse ROI tracked, steers investment
anchors.L5: Reuse/ROI a leadership-visible metric guiding the portfolio

probing_questions.q: Do you measure how often core skills/components are reused?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether reuse is tracked at all. Strong: reuse rate measured. Weak: unmeasured → reuse stays incidental.

probing_questions.q: Can you show time-to-build reduction from reuse?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes tangible leverage evidence. Strong: demonstrated build-time reduction. Weak: no data → can't prove value.

probing_questions.q: Is reuse ROI tracked and used to steer investment?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether measurement drives decisions. Strong: ROI steers investment. Weak: not tracked → no funding case for the platform/CoE.

probing_questions.q: What share of new work/agents is assembled mostly from existing skills?
probing_questions.looking_for: A maturity proxy for compounding. Strong: a high share assembled from existing skills. Weak: mostly built fresh.

nodes.label: 2.7 Operating Model, Ownership & Incentives
nodes.summary: Tooling exists everywhere; reuse fails without ownership and a sharing culture.

anchors.L3: Named owner (CoE/platform); basic standards
anchors.L4: Incentives to contribute/reuse; active sharing culture
anchors.L5: Self-sustaining community; reuse is the cultural default; library treated as strategic asset

probing_questions.q: Who owns the skills/knowledge function (CoE, platform team)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests for clear ownership of the asset base. Strong: a named owner/CoE. Weak: nobody → the library rots.

probing_questions.q: Are people incentivized to contribute and reuse vs. build their own?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes incentives (reuse fails without them). Strong: contribution/reuse rewarded. Weak: rewarded only for building new → hoarding.

probing_questions.q: Is there a sharing culture, or do teams hoard/duplicate?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests cultural readiness for reuse. Strong: sharing is the norm. Weak: hoarding/not-invented-here → duplication.

probing_questions.q: Does leadership treat the skill library as a strategic asset?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether the moat is recognized at the top. Strong: treated as strategic and funded. Weak: seen as a side project → underinvested.

nodes.label: Dimension 3: Data, Knowledge Sources & Retrieval
nodes.summary: Assessment dimension 3 of the nine-dimension maturity model: Data, Knowledge Sources & Retrieval. Contains 6 criteria scored L1-L5.

nodes.label: 3.1 Proprietary Data Richness & Strategic Fit
nodes.summary: Proprietary data is the durable moat once models commoditize; richness tells you where to play.

anchors.L1: Data edge unknown; generic use cases
anchors.L2: Aware of some rich data, not assessed
anchors.L3: Richness scored across domains; bets aligned to richest data
anchors.L4: Richness actively steers the portfolio
anchors.L5: Rich proprietary data managed as a strategic moat

probing_questions.q: Where is your data genuinely richer than competitors' (domain specificity, frequency, depth, exclusivity)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests awareness of the real moat. Strong: specific, differentiated data identified. Weak: 'we have lots of data' with no edge → generic, copyable use cases.

probing_questions.q: Have you scored data richness across your domains (customer / operational / administrative / risk)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes deliberate richness mapping (AI Radar). Strong: a richness assessment exists. Weak: never assessed → bets aimed at convenient, not rich, data.

probing_questions.q: Are AI bets aimed at your richest data, or at whatever's convenient?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests strategic fit of data to use cases. Strong: bets concentrated on rich data. Weak: data-poor bets → no advantage.

probing_questions.q: What data could only you have?
probing_questions.looking_for: Surfaces the exclusivity that underpins durable advantage. Strong: a clear answer. Weak: none → no proprietary edge.

nodes.label: 3.2 Knowledge Source Inventory, Ownership & Freshness
nodes.summary: Unowned/stale sources are the root of confidently-wrong output; ownership separates Achievers from Discoverers.

anchors.L3: Key sources inventoried, owned, refreshed
anchors.L4: Owners + cadence enterprise-wide; trust signalled
anchors.L5: Continuous source curation; freshness/trust assured by design

probing_questions.q: Have you inventoried the knowledge sources agents will draw on?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether sources are even known. Strong: a maintained inventory. Weak: unknown/scattered → agents ground on whatever's handy.

probing_questions.q: Does each critical source have a named owner and a refresh cadence?
probing_questions.looking_for: Ownership separates Achievers from Discoverers. Strong: named owners + cadence. Weak: unowned sources → drift and contradictions.

probing_questions.q: How do you know a source is current and trustworthy?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes freshness/trust signals. Strong: freshness tracked, trust signalled. Weak: no way to tell → confidently-wrong output.

probing_questions.q: How much critical knowledge lives only in people's heads or scattered files?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the dark-knowledge gap. Strong: most critical knowledge captured in usable sources. Weak: key knowledge is tacit/scattered → inaccessible to agents.

nodes.label: 3.3 Data Accessibility & Integration (fit-for-purpose)
nodes.summary: MCP, APIs and event streaming solve different layers; maturity is fit-for-purpose selection, not 'everything via MCP.'

anchors.L2: Some sources connected for pilots; pattern ad-hoc
anchors.L3: Key sources accessible; APIs managed; MCP for agent tool-use over existing APIs
anchors.L4: Fit-for-purpose: event backbone + managed APIs + MCP agent layer + A2A; unstructured accessible; data products
anchors.L5: Standardized, governed, observable agent-access layer over a durable event/API backbone; right pattern per job

probing_questions.q: Can agents access structured AND unstructured data across systems?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests reach across the ~80% that is unstructured. Strong: both accessible. Weak: only structured/siloed → agents see a fraction of context.

probing_questions.q: Do you select integration patterns by fit — event backbone for async/high-volume, managed APIs for deterministic/compliance, MCP for agent tool-use (rule of thumb: MCP when 3+ integrations feed an AI workflow)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests architectural judgment. Strong: fit-for-purpose pattern selection. Weak: one-size-fits-all → wrong tool for the job.

probing_questions.q: Is MCP layered OVER your existing API/event backbone (wrapping APIs), or are you trying to replace integration with MCP?
probing_questions.looking_for: Catches the 'MCP-for-everything' anti-pattern. Strong: MCP as the agent-access layer over a sound backbone. Weak: routing deterministic/high-volume/compliance flows through MCP → latency, cost, non-determinism, compliance risk.

probing_questions.q: How do you handle async, reliability, and LLM-specific failures (queues, dead-letter queues) in agent workflows?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests resilience of the integration substrate. Strong: durable event backbone + DLQs. Weak: brittle synchronous chains → data loss, stalls.

nodes.label: 3.4 Data Quality & Readiness
nodes.summary: 'Relying on the knowledge source without governing its quality produces confident but unreliable systems.'

anchors.L3: Quality/freshness assured for priority sources; retrieval-ready
anchors.L4: Quality SLAs; low latency; structured/labeled at scale
anchors.L5: Continuous, automated quality + freshness; readiness by design

probing_questions.q: What is the quality/freshness of the data agents rely on, and how is it assured?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests quality assurance. Strong: assured quality/freshness. Weak: unmanaged → garbage-in at machine scale, hallucinations.

probing_questions.q: Is data appropriately structured/labeled for retrieval?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes retrieval-readiness. Strong: structured/labeled/chunked for use. Weak: raw dumps → poor retrieval.

probing_questions.q: What's the latency between source-of-truth and what the agent sees?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests staleness risk. Strong: low, understood latency. Weak: unknown/high → agents act on stale data.

probing_questions.q: Are you delaying value waiting for 'perfect' data you may not need?
probing_questions.looking_for: Guards against the over-correction (availability has diminishing returns). Strong: pragmatic 'good-enough' threshold. Weak: endless cleanup before any value.

nodes.label: 3.5 Retrieval & Context Engineering (RAG, grounding)
nodes.summary: The agent-specific core: a context-first architecture is what turns pilots into production.

anchors.L2: Basic RAG; flat vector store, no eval
anchors.L3: Governed RAG over key sources
anchors.L4: Agentic RAG; domain-tuned embeddings; grounding measured
anchors.L5: Context-first architecture; knowledge graph + agentic RAG; grounding continuously optimized

probing_questions.q: How do agents retrieve and assemble context (RAG, knowledge graph, embeddings)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the agent-specific core. Strong: a deliberate retrieval architecture. Weak: raw prompts/no retrieval → ungrounded answers.

probing_questions.q: Is retrieval governed and evaluated, or a flat vector dump?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes retrieval quality discipline. Strong: governed, measured retrieval (agentic RAG). Weak: flat vector store, no eval → confident but unreliable.

probing_questions.q: Do you tune embeddings/chunking for your domain?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests precision of grounding. Strong: domain-tuned embeddings/chunking. Weak: generic defaults → poor recall/precision.

probing_questions.q: How do you measure and reduce hallucination/grounding failures?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether grounding quality is managed. Strong: grounding metrics + remediation. Weak: no measurement → silent failures.

nodes.label: 3.6 Data Governance, Privacy & Rights for AI/Agent Use
aliases: Data Governance, Privacy & Rights for AI/Agent Use
nodes.summary: Governance hasn't scaled with data distribution; unstructured data is especially exposed.

anchors.L3: Classification + access control for priority AI data
anchors.L4: Consent/rights enforced; access traceable; unstructured covered
anchors.L5: Governance scaled to AI's reach; continuous, automated, auditable

probing_questions.q: Is data classified and access-controlled for AI use cases (including unstructured)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests AI-specific data governance. Strong: classification + access control incl. unstructured. Weak: ungoverned → over-retrieval, leaks.

probing_questions.q: Do you enforce consent/usage rights on data fed to agents?
probing_questions.looking_for: Probes rights/consent. Strong: rights enforced on agent inputs. Weak: none → privacy/regulatory breach.

probing_questions.q: Can you trace what data an agent accessed and why?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests data-access traceability. Strong: traceable access. Weak: invisible access → undetectable breaches.

probing_questions.q: Has governance scaled to match AI's reach into your data?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether governance kept pace with AI adoption. Strong: governance scaled with AI. Weak: governance lagging → growing exposure.

nodes.label: Dimension 4: Agent Platform, Harness Engineering & Operations (incl. Autonomy)
aliases: Agent Platform, Harness Engineering & Operations (incl. Autonomy)
nodes.summary: Assessment dimension 4 of the nine-dimension maturity model: Agent Platform, Harness Engineering & Operations (incl. Autonomy). Contains 6 criteria scored L1-L5.

nodes.label: 4.1 Use-Case Selection & Pattern Fit
nodes.summary: Not every process needs an agent; pattern over-reach is a top cause of cost and failure.

anchors.L1: 'Everything is an agent'; no decision framework
anchors.L3: Decision framework applied (intelligence vs reliability; agent-or-not); simplest pattern matched
anchors.L4: Pattern fit governs the portfolio; deterministic/human-in-loop chosen where right
anchors.L5: Disciplined pattern selection org-wide; the agent is what remains after deterministic extraction

probing_questions.q: For each candidate, do you ask 'does this need intelligence or reliability?' and 'does this need to be an agent at all?' before building?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the decision discipline. Strong: an explicit decision framework; deterministic workflow / human-in-loop are valid outcomes. Weak: 'everything is an agent' → wrong tool, cost, failure.

probing_questions.q: Can you prove the required accuracy with evaluation data, and are errors recoverable and detectable?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests fitness-for-agent. Strong: accuracy provable, errors recoverable/detectable. Weak: unprovable accuracy or undetectable high-impact errors → should not be an autonomous agent.

probing_questions.q: Do you match the simplest pattern (LLM-as-function -> single -> hybrid -> subagent -> multi), or default to 'an agent' / 'multi-agent'?
probing_questions.looking_for: Guards against pattern over-reach. Strong: simplest pattern that works. Weak: multi-agent by default → cost, coordination failure.

probing_questions.q: Are deterministic workflow and human-in-loop assistant treated as valid (often preferred) outcomes?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests honesty about where AI fits. Strong: yes, and chosen often. Weak: agents forced onto deterministic work → fragility dressed up as autonomy.

nodes.label: 4.2 Harness, Skills & Runtime Strategy
nodes.summary: ~75-80% of value is in skill-based augmentation agents, and they are the on-ramp to autonomy.

anchors.L1: Bespoke autonomous builds; skills not leveraged
anchors.L3: Helper skills built upward into closed loops; portable skills
anchors.L4: Skill-based agents the primary engine; local->centralized promotion path
anchors.L5: Local agents promoted to a centralized runtime where justified; skills portable/build-to-delete

probing_questions.q: Are you leveraging harness agents (Claude Code/Cowork + plugins + skills) as a primary value engine?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests capture of the ~75-80% near-term value. Strong: skill-based agents are a primary engine. Weak: chasing bespoke autonomous builds → misses the real value.

probing_questions.q: Do you build UPWARD from small, genuinely-used helper skills into a worker's closed loop, or script big agents top-down?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests build direction. Strong: upward from used helpers. Weak: top-down process scripting → stalls (tacit knowledge never captured).

probing_questions.q: Are skills/plugins portable and tool-independent (build-to-delete)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests durability of the asset vs the tool. Strong: skills move across tools intact. Weak: locked to one platform → rework when the tool turns over.

probing_questions.q: Is there a path to assemble local agents and promote them to a centralized/managed runtime as they mature?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the on-ramp to autonomy. Strong: a clear local->centralized promotion path. Weak: no path → local agents never graduate safely.

nodes.label: 4.3 Agent Architecture & Context Engineering
nodes.summary: Architecture determines reliability; accuracy compounds negatively across chained agents; it's all context.

anchors.L3: Single-agent-first; hybrid extraction; context designed first
anchors.L4: Deliberate patterns; function/events/MCP/durable-execution used correctly
anchors.L5: Reliable hybrid architectures; context-first; reusable, observable design

probing_questions.q: Do you start with a single agent and maximize it before adding agents, and avoid chaining within a domain?
probing_questions.looking_for: 'Accuracy compounds negatively across chained agents.' Strong: single-first, no needless chaining. Weak: agent sprawl → context loss at handoffs.

probing_questions.q: Do you extract deterministic steps into a workflow and keep the agent only at judgment points (hybrid)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the hybrid pattern. Strong: deterministic steps in code, agent at judgment. Weak: agent does everything → fragile, costly.

probing_questions.q: Is context engineering treated as the primary lever (what the model sees), with memory/RAG/tools as utilities?
probing_questions.looking_for: 'It's all context.' Strong: context designed first. Weak: infrastructure built first, context an afterthought → poor quality.

probing_questions.q: How do agents integrate — function calling for actions, events for outcomes, MCP for shared tools, durable execution for orchestration?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests integration design. Strong: right mechanism per job; ambient agents event-driven. Weak: brittle synchronous chains / API rebuilds for agents.

nodes.label: 4.4 Graduation to Autonomy (in-loop -> operator -> out-of-loop)
nodes.summary: Autonomy is earned through a gate, not pursued; most work is most valuable in-loop/operator.

anchors.L3: Stages explicit; autonomy case-by-case; most work stays in-loop/operator
anchors.L4: Four-condition gate governs graduation; augmentation-first; reversible
anchors.L5: Gated, reversible, audited graduation; out-of-loop only where proven; centralized runtime keeps it safe

probing_questions.q: Do you treat the path as in-loop -> operator -> out-of-loop, with most work staying in-loop/operator by design?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the graduation mindset. Strong: stages explicit; most work stops early by design. Weak: out-of-loop treated as the goal → autonomous-first failure.

probing_questions.q: Is autonomy earned through the four-condition gate (stable pattern; bounded failure cost; evaluable; volume & leverage)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the gate. Strong: all four required before graduating. Weak: autonomy granted on enthusiasm → high-impact failures.

probing_questions.q: Is graduation reversible — do you pull work back when conditions no longer hold?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests governance of autonomy. Strong: work is pulled back when it starts failing. Weak: one-way promotion → silent drift into failure.

probing_questions.q: Does a centralized runtime/harness make out-of-loop safe (guardrails, human checkpoints, audit)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests safe-autonomy infrastructure. Strong: out-of-loop runs with guardrails/checkpoints/audit. Weak: autonomy without a safety harness → uncontained risk.

nodes.label: 4.5 Evaluation & Quality (Evals)
nodes.summary: If judging needs a human on every instance, no autonomous version could know it had gone wrong.

anchors.L3: Eval suite + regression for priority agents
anchors.L4: Tiered evals gate releases; distribution tested; failures feed back
anchors.L5: Evals + trajectory feedback drive continuous improvement; the gate's 'evaluable' condition is met by design

probing_questions.q: How do you evaluate agents — eval suites, scored traces, regression tests?
probing_questions.looking_for: Evals are quality AND the gate's 'evaluable' condition. Strong: real eval suites + regression. Weak: demos/spot-checks → nothing can credibly graduate.

probing_questions.q: Can you objectively tell if the work was done correctly across ordinary, edge, and worst cases?
probing_questions.looking_for: The evaluable condition. Strong: objective judging incl. edges/worst cases. Weak: needs a human on every instance → no safe autonomy possible.

probing_questions.q: Do you tier evals by cost/speed (commit / PR / pre-deploy / production)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests practical eval discipline. Strong: tiered evals. Weak: all-or-nothing → evals skipped under pressure.

probing_questions.q: Do production failures become regression tests, and do you test the distribution, not the happy path?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the closed quality loop + non-determinism. Strong: failures -> regressions; distribution tested. Weak: happy-path only → silent tail failures.

nodes.label: 4.6 AgentOps: Observability, Reliability, Cost & Trajectory Capture
aliases: AgentOps: Observability, Reliability, Cost & Trajectory Capture
nodes.summary: Agents fail invisibly; unconstrained loops/fleets and cost are production risks; trajectories are the improvement dataset.

anchors.L3: Structured tracing + basic reliability for priority agents
anchors.L4: Full tracing across handoffs; circuit breakers/loop guards/fleet supervision; gateway cost control; drift detection
anchors.L5: Always-on observability + reliability + cost optimization; trajectories feed the flywheel

probing_questions.q: Do you trace every model/tool/retrieval/reasoning step as structured spans across handoffs?
probing_questions.looking_for: Agents fail in ways that look like success. Strong: nested structured tracing. Weak: black-box → undetected failures.

probing_questions.q: Do you enforce circuit breakers, loop guards, iteration/token limits, and fleet supervision?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests reliability controls. Strong: loops/fleets bounded and supervised. Weak: runaway loops/cost, no fleet view.

probing_questions.q: Do you track semantic SLIs and detect drift (action / policy / trigger / learning)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests behavioral monitoring. Strong: drift detected on baselines. Weak: only infra metrics → slow divergence unnoticed.

probing_questions.q: Is cost governed via a gateway, and are trajectories captured and fed back (link to Dim 2)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests cost control + the flywheel. Strong: central gateway + trajectory capture feeding improvement. Weak: fragmented cost, no trajectory data.

nodes.label: Dimension 5: Agentic Platform & Control Plane (Operating Model)
nodes.summary: Assessment dimension 5 of the nine-dimension maturity model: Agentic Platform & Control Plane (Operating Model). Contains 8 criteria scored L1-L5.

nodes.label: 5.1 Platform Ownership & Platform-as-Product
nodes.summary: An unowned, project-run platform decays; product management sustains adoption. (Score outcome, not org chart.)

anchors.L1: No clear owner; conflated with data/AI
anchors.L2: Owner emerging; run as a side project
anchors.L3: Clear agentic-platform ownership; basic roadmap/support
anchors.L4: Run as a product: roadmap, SLAs, users, funded
anchors.L5: Funded product driving adoption; primitives fully owned

probing_questions.q: Who owns the agentic platform today, and is it distinct from your data/AI platforms?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests clear ownership of an AGENTIC platform. Strong: a clear owner, distinct from (but aligned to) data/AI platforms. Weak: no owner, or conflated with a generic AI/data platform.

probing_questions.q: Is the platform run as a product (roadmap, SLAs, named internal users, support), or as a side project?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests platform-as-product maturity. Strong: product-managed with users and support. Weak: ad-hoc/project. (Score on a spectrum; early-stage orgs legitimately aren't here yet.)

probing_questions.q: Does the owning team understand and own the platform primitives (harness, runtime, registry, gateways, tools)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests depth of ownership. Strong: primitives clearly owned and understood. Weak: primitives scattered/unowned.

probing_questions.q: How is platform investment funded and prioritized against demand?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests sustainability. Strong: funded, demand-driven roadmap. Weak: unfunded/reactive → platform decays.

nodes.label: 5.2 Golden Paths & Build/Run Operating Model
nodes.summary: Without a paved path and enablement, every team improvises and the platform goes unused.

anchors.L3: Golden path for main deployment types; enabler team helps
anchors.L4: Paved paths across deployment types; clear platform<->squad model; enablement builds self-sufficiency
anchors.L5: Self-service golden paths; embedded enablement; teams ship independently

probing_questions.q: How does a team go from idea to a deployed agent today — a paved golden path, or bespoke each time?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the paved road. Strong: a repeatable golden path. Weak: every team improvises end-to-end.

probing_questions.q: Does the golden path cover the deployment types you actually use (local harness, managed remote, SDK, multi-agent)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests coverage. Strong: covers the relevant types. Weak: one-size-fits-all or gaps → teams go off-road.

probing_questions.q: Who is allowed to build agents — central team only, federated builders, or both — and is that deliberate?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the build model. Strong: a deliberate model fit to context. Weak: unclear/accidental → bottleneck or sprawl.

probing_questions.q: Is there an enabler/tiger team that helps others author skills and agents, and does it transfer capability (build WITH, not FOR)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests enablement that creates self-sufficiency. Strong: embeds and makes teams self-sufficient. Weak: none, or a central bottleneck.

probing_questions.q: What is the working/interaction model between the platform team and the squads/pods building agents?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests platform<->consumer relationship. Strong: clear support/paved-road model. Weak: throw-over-the-wall or no relationship.

nodes.label: 5.3 Governed Use-Case & PoC Intake
nodes.summary: Ungoverned intake is the source of PoC sprawl; the gate enforces Dim 4.1/Dim 1 criteria.

anchors.L3: Managed gate applies agent-or-not & value criteria
anchors.L4: Autonomy level decided + validated at the gate; portfolio actively managed (kill/scale)
anchors.L5: Disciplined intake; no sprawl; gate prevents low-value builds

probing_questions.q: How are candidate agent use cases intake'd and decided — a managed gate, or do PoCs start anywhere?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests intake governance. Strong: a managed intake/gate. Weak: anyone starts a PoC → sprawl.

probing_questions.q: Does the gate apply the selection criteria (agent-or-not, business value, autonomy level) BEFORE work starts?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests up-front rigor (criteria defined in Dim 4.1/Dim 1). Strong: criteria enforced at the gate. Weak: built first, justified later.

probing_questions.q: How do you prevent PoC sprawl — is the PoC portfolio actively managed, with kill/scale decisions?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests portfolio discipline. Strong: managed portfolio, things get killed. Weak: PoCs accumulate, nothing killed.

probing_questions.q: Is the target autonomy level decided at the gate (via a quick validation PoC), or discovered later in dev/deploy?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests when autonomy is decided. Strong: decided + validated at the gate. Weak: emerges late → rework, risk.

nodes.label: 5.4 Reference Patterns & Architectural Governance by Agent Type/Autonomy
aliases: Reference Patterns & Architectural Governance by Agent Type/Autonomy
nodes.summary: Standardized patterns per type/autonomy make builds reliable and govern churn; fuzzy types cause misaligned builds.

anchors.L3: Documented patterns per type/autonomy; types clearly defined
anchors.L4: Architectural governance used; framework/runtime/harness decision guide; stable-vs-moving guidance
anchors.L5: Mature pattern catalog + lightweight governance; build-to-delete isolates churn from durable assets

probing_questions.q: Do you have documented, standardized design patterns / reference architectures per agent type and autonomy level?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests a pattern catalog. Strong: a maintained, used catalog. Weak: every build improvises architecture.

probing_questions.q: Are the agent types clearly defined (augmentation, AI assistant, task-based autonomous, in/on/out-of-loop, conversational, multi-turn conversational)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests shared vocabulary. Strong: clear definitions teams use. Weak: fuzzy/overloaded terms → misaligned builds.

probing_questions.q: Is there architectural governance (review against the patterns) used without becoming a bottleneck?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests lightweight governance. Strong: used and proportionate. Weak: none, or a heavy gate everyone bypasses.

probing_questions.q: What dictates the choice of framework, runtime, and harness for a given agent — a documented decision guide or individual preference?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests decision discipline. Strong: a decision guide tied to type/autonomy. Weak: per-person preference → fragmentation.

probing_questions.q: How do you guide teams to bet on STABLE components vs the fast-moving parts (models/frameworks change ~every 6 months)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests adaptability/build-to-delete. Strong: explicit stable-vs-moving guidance; durable assets isolated from churn. Weak: no guidance → rework every cycle.

nodes.label: 5.5 Control-Plane Primitives: Registry, Identity, Gateways & Observability
aliases: Control-Plane Primitives: Registry, Identity, Gateways & Observability
nodes.summary: Registry, identity, gateways and multi-purpose observability make a fleet governable, affordable and safe.

anchors.L2: Partial inventory; basic logging; ad-hoc gateway
anchors.L3: Registry + per-agent identity for priority agents; an AI gateway in place
anchors.L4: AI gateway (cost/routing/policy) + MCP gateway; observability serves monitoring/evals/cost
anchors.L5: Consolidated gateways (AI/MCP/API); least-privilege identity; observability serves monitoring, logging, security, evals, cost, drift fleet-wide

probing_questions.q: Is there an agent registry/inventory (what agents exist, owners, scope, status)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests fleet visibility. Strong: a maintained registry. Weak: no inventory → shadow agents.

probing_questions.q: Do agents have managed identity and least-privilege access as a platform primitive?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the access primitive (security DEPTH = Dim 8). Strong: per-agent identity/least-privilege from the platform. Weak: shared/blanket credentials.

probing_questions.q: Do you have an AI/LLM gateway, and what is it leveraged for (cost attribution, routing, caching, rate-limiting, policy/guardrail enforcement)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the central chokepoint. Strong: a gateway used for cost + routing + policy. Weak: fragmented LLM access, cost blind spots, no policy enforcement point.

probing_questions.q: Which gateways are in place (AI/LLM, MCP, API), and does the AI gateway also serve as the MCP gateway (e.g., via plugins) — how consolidated are they?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests gateway taxonomy & consolidation. Strong: deliberate set of gateways (incl. an MCP gateway governing tool/MCP-server traffic), consciously consolidated. Weak: only a traditional API gateway, no MCP-traffic governance, accidental sprawl.

probing_questions.q: What is your agentic observability leveraged for — continuous monitoring, logging, security, evals, cost, and drift?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests observability BREADTH. Strong: observability feeds monitoring, evals, security, cost, and drift. Weak: latency/logs only → blind to silent failures, drift, abuse.

nodes.label: 5.6 Orchestration, Durable-Execution Runtime & Tooling/Connector Catalog
nodes.summary: Long-running/Deep agents must survive failures via durable execution; shared orchestration + a governed tool catalog let agents act and coordinate reliably at scale.

anchors.L1: No orchestration runtime; agents restart on failure; bespoke tools per agent
anchors.L2: Some workflow glue; tools duplicated; no durable execution
anchors.L3: Orchestration for priority flows; a tool/connector catalog emerging
anchors.L4: Managed orchestration + durable execution (state persistence/resume) for long-running agents; governed shared tool/MCP-server catalog with standards
anchors.L5: Platform durable-execution runtime (Deep agents survive failures); discoverable, versioned tool catalog; orchestration + reasoning as clean complementary layers

probing_questions.q: Does the platform provide a managed orchestration runtime for multi-step / multi-agent (A2A) coordination, or does each team build its own?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests shared orchestration. Strong: a platform orchestration runtime. Weak: bespoke orchestration per team → fragmentation.

probing_questions.q: For long-running / Deep agents, is there a durable-execution platform so they survive failures and resume (state persistence, recovery) rather than restart?
probing_questions.looking_for: THE key primitive for Deep agents. Strong: durable execution (e.g., Temporal-style or managed runtime with resumable state). Weak: long-running agents restart from scratch / must be babysat → unreliable.

probing_questions.q: Is there a shared, governed tool/connector/MCP-server catalog (adapters, discovery, versioning)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the tool catalog. Strong: a discoverable, versioned catalog of vetted tools/connectors. Weak: bespoke tools rebuilt per agent.

probing_questions.q: Are tool sets kept small and task-relevant, with tool-design standards (clear function signatures, designed from the agent's perspective)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests tool-design discipline (adapters are the primary driver of agent reliability). Strong: small, task-scoped tools with standards. Weak: agents handed large API catalogs → worse performance.

probing_questions.q: Is durable execution / orchestration treated as a complementary layer to the agent's reasoning loop, not conflated with it?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests architectural clarity. Strong: durable-execution platform + agent framework as separate, complementary layers. Weak: orchestration and reasoning tangled → brittle, hard to operate.

nodes.label: 5.7 Interoperability, Integration & Build-vs-Buy / Topology
nodes.summary: Standardized integration and deliberate build/buy prevent fragmentation and accidental multi-platform sprawl.

anchors.L1: Bespoke integration per agent; accidental platforms
anchors.L3: Standardized integration patterns; build/buy considered
anchors.L4: Deliberate build/buy rule; intentional deployment topology
anchors.L5: Consistent, reusable integration across the estate; intentional, optimized topology

probing_questions.q: Does the platform provide standardized patterns for integrating with enterprise systems (events, APIs, message bus), or does each team wire its own?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests reusable enterprise integration. Strong: standardized, reusable patterns. Weak: bespoke per agent.

probing_questions.q: How do you decide build vs buy for platform primitives (harness, gateways, registry, orchestration, eval tooling)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests sourcing discipline. Strong: a deliberate build/buy rule. Weak: accidental/duplicated builds.

probing_questions.q: What is your deployment topology — managed harness, cloud agent platform, home-built, or a mix — and is the mix intentional?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests topology intent. Strong: an intentional topology with rationale. Weak: accidental multi-platform sprawl.

probing_questions.q: Are integration and platform patterns consistent across deployment types and teams?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests consistency. Strong: consistent across the estate. Weak: fragmented → rework, brittle integration.

nodes.label: 5.8 Cross-Team Alignment (Governance, Data, Quality)
nodes.summary: A platform misaligned with governance, data, and quality produces ungoverned, ungrounded, low-accuracy agents.

anchors.L3: Regular alignment with governance and data
anchors.L4: Governance paved into the platform; data access joint; quality gating with accuracy improvement
anchors.L5: Shared roadmap/rhythms; governance, data and quality embedded in the platform by design

probing_questions.q: How aligned are the platform team and the governance body — are guardrails/policies built INTO the platform (paved), or bolted on later?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests governance-by-design. Strong: governance embedded in the golden path. Weak: governance separate/after-the-fact → bypassed.

probing_questions.q: How aligned are the platform team and the data/document teams (the agentic platform needs governed data/document access)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests platform<->data alignment (capability itself = Dim 3). Strong: joint ownership of knowledge access. Weak: siloed → agents can't reach data.

probing_questions.q: Is there an evals/quality gating function, with an accuracy threshold and a continuous-improvement process tied to the platform?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests quality as a platform function (eval practice = Dim 4.5). Strong: quality gating + accuracy improves over time through usage. Weak: no quality function → accuracy stagnates.

probing_questions.q: Do these teams share roadmap and operating rhythms, or operate independently?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests operating-rhythm alignment. Strong: shared rhythms/roadmap. Weak: independent → drift and misalignment.

nodes.label: Dimension 6: Agentic Workflow Redesign & Human-AI Pairing
nodes.summary: Assessment dimension 6 of the nine-dimension maturity model: Agentic Workflow Redesign & Human-AI Pairing. Contains 7 criteria scored L1-L5.

nodes.label: 6.1 Locating the Agentic Insertion Point
nodes.summary: The agentic part is where judgment lives; that's the only part this transformation touches. Generic mapping/mining is out of scope.

anchors.L3: Judgment step located; only it is redesigned
anchors.L4: Clear intelligence-vs-rules test applied per step
anchors.L5: Agentic insertion points precisely targeted; deterministic work left alone by design

probing_questions.q: How does the team decide, across candidate processes, where an LLM/agent genuinely adds judgment value vs. where work is deterministic — is this a repeatable, evidenced practice or ad-hoc per person?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests maturity of the targeting practice. Strong: a standard, shared method applied consistently with evidence. Weak: gut feel that varies by individual.

probing_questions.q: When the team scopes an agentic initiative, how consistently do they isolate the specific judgment step(s) rather than targeting the whole process?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests scope discipline as a team norm. Strong: scoping to the judgment step is the default. Weak: 'agentify the whole process' is the habit.

probing_questions.q: What test or criteria does the team use to confirm a step needs reasoning (not just rules), and is it documented and shared?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests for a repeatable intelligence-vs-rules test. Strong: a documented, shared test. Weak: none — assumes an LLM is needed everywhere.

probing_questions.q: How does the team keep this focused on agentic value rather than sliding into generic process mapping / process mining?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests scope maturity. Strong: deliberate discipline to stay on the agentic value point. Weak: scope creep into generic BPM.

nodes.label: 6.2 Error Reversibility & Recovery-Cost Assessment
nodes.summary: If errors are undetectable or irreversible with high/impossible recovery cost, an autonomous agent is the wrong choice; recovery cost is part of agentic TCO.

anchors.L1: Reversibility/recovery cost not considered; agents act on irreversible steps
anchors.L3: Detectability/reversibility/recovery-cost assessed for priority steps and drives design
anchors.L4: Standard: irreversible/high-cost actions behind checkpoints or human-in-loop; recovery cost in TCO
anchors.L5: Disciplined gate input across the portfolio; continuously re-evaluated; feeds intake (5.3) and TCO (1.5)

probing_questions.q: When designing an agentic step, does the team systematically assess whether errors are DETECTABLE and REVERSIBLE, and the COST/possibility of recovery — or is this overlooked?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the reversibility discipline. Strong: a standard assessment of detectability, reversibility, and recovery cost. Weak: not considered until something goes wrong.

probing_questions.q: Does that assessment DRIVE the design (deterministic-vs-agentic, pairing mode, agent-or-not), or is it considered only after build?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests whether it actually gates design. Strong: reversibility/cost shapes the design up front. Weak: bolted on / rationalized after the fact.

probing_questions.q: For irreversible or high-recovery-cost actions, does the team keep a human in the loop or place the irreversible step behind a human checkpoint, as a standard?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests safe design for irreversibility. Strong: irreversible steps behind a checkpoint / human-in-loop by default. Weak: autonomous agents act on irreversible, high-cost steps.

probing_questions.q: Is error-recovery cost included in the agent's total cost of ownership (and fed to the intake gate / Dim 1.5)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests cost honesty. Strong: recovery cost counted in TCO and at the gate. Weak: recovery cost ignored → TCO understated, bad go/no-go calls.

nodes.label: 6.3 Deterministic <-> Agentic Composition
nodes.summary: Composition keeps the agentic workflow evaluable and auditable; over-agentifying or blind automation both fail.

anchors.L3: Agent scoped to judgment; deterministic shell around it
anchors.L4: Anti-patterns avoided (no re-agentifying BPA; augmentation-first where right)
anchors.L5: Clean deterministic<->agentic composition; workflow orchestrates, agent judges

probing_questions.q: As a standard, how does the team compose deterministic steps (sequencing/validation/routing) with the agentic judgment step — a shared pattern, or does each build differ?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests for a reusable composition pattern. Strong: a shared, reused pattern. Weak: every build improvises the boundary.

probing_questions.q: How consistently does the team recognize and avoid over-agentifying work already handled by deterministic automation — is there an explicit reliability-vs-intelligence check?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests maturity against anti-pattern 1. Strong: an explicit check; deterministic work stays deterministic. Weak: routinely re-agentifies working BPA/RPA.

probing_questions.q: For work that doesn't need agent intelligence, is 'augment people first, earn trust through use' an established team practice, or is blind automation the default?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests maturity against anti-pattern 2. Strong: augmentation-first is the norm. Weak: defaults to blind automation.

probing_questions.q: How clearly and consistently does the team separate orchestration (workflow/durable execution) from the agent's judgment role across its builds?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests architectural maturity. Strong: consistent separation. Weak: agents routinely try to run the whole flow.

nodes.label: 6.4 Human-AI Pairing Mode & Its Control Mechanism
aliases: Human-AI Pairing Mode & Its Control Mechanism
nodes.summary: Each mode has a different required control; choosing a mode without its mechanism is the common failure. (On-loop = real-time escalation; out-of-loop = after-the-fact review.)

anchors.L1: Mode chosen with no mechanism (e.g., out-of-loop, no after-the-fact check)
anchors.L3: Each mode has its required mechanism built (real-time escalation / after-the-fact sampling / skill-triggered augmentation)
anchors.L4: Mechanisms robust; user truly orchestrates via skills in-loop; escalation + post-hoc validation reliable
anchors.L5: Pairing mechanisms re-calibrated from usage; right mode + mechanism by design

probing_questions.q: How mature is the team at selecting the pairing mode (in/on/out-of-loop) per agentic step AND building its required control mechanism — standardized, or case-by-case?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests mode+mechanism maturity. Strong: a standard practice where each mode ships with its mechanism. Weak: mode labels chosen, mechanisms missing.

probing_questions.q: For in-the-loop augmentation, how consistently does the team deliver skills the user can trigger and orchestrate the workflow through (vs. tools the user can't really drive)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests augmentation maturity. Strong: skill-triggered, user-orchestrated augmentation as a norm. Weak: nominal 'augmentation' the user can't actually drive.

probing_questions.q: For on-the-loop work (the agent acts autonomously under REAL-TIME human monitoring, with the ability to intervene), does the team have a standard, reusable escalation/intervention procedure (who/when/how) applied across builds?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests supervised-autonomy maturity. On-the-loop = the human watches in real time and steps in on exceptions AS THEY HAPPEN. Strong: a reusable real-time escalation/intervention pattern. Weak: ad-hoc or absent.

probing_questions.q: For out-of-the-loop work (the agent runs fully autonomously with NO real-time oversight), does the team have an established AFTER-THE-FACT validation practice (scanning/sampling via tooling, audit/logs) plus an escalation path for cases the agent itself flags?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests safe-autonomy maturity. Out-of-the-loop = no runtime oversight; control is after-the-fact. Strong: standard post-hoc sampling/scanning + escalation path. Weak: autonomy shipped with no after-the-fact check.

nodes.label: 6.5 Eval Loop & Reasoning Capture
nodes.summary: Capturing reasoning makes the agentic step improvable, auditable, and a candidate for graduation.

anchors.L3: Eval loop + reasoning (accept/override/escalate) captured
anchors.L4: Reasoning feeds quality + the flywheel; decisions auditable
anchors.L5: Reasoning capture is a managed asset driving improvement and trust

probing_questions.q: How established is the team's practice of building an eval loop for the agentic/judgment step — a standard, or only on some builds?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests eval maturity. Strong: eval loops are standard for agentic steps. Weak: ad-hoc or absent.

probing_questions.q: How systematically does the team capture the reasoning (accept/override/decline/delegate/escalate, with the why) — not just outcomes — across agentic workflows?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests judgment-capture maturity. Strong: systematic reasoning capture. Weak: only outcomes logged; reasoning lost.

probing_questions.q: Is captured reasoning consistently routed into quality improvement and the knowledge flywheel (Dim 2), or does it sit unused?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the link to the moat. Strong: consistently fed back. Weak: captured-but-unused, or not captured.

probing_questions.q: How auditable are the team's agentic decisions by design — is explainability/auditability a standard, or retrofitted case-by-case?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests auditability maturity. Strong: auditable by design. Weak: black-box, retrofitted under pressure.

nodes.label: 6.6 Improvement Flywheel & Continuous Agentic Redesign
nodes.summary: Trust and accuracy are earned through usage and continuous improvement; override rate is the key signal.

anchors.L1: Static agentic step; no signal-driven refinement
anchors.L3: Usage signals drive refinement; override rate tracked
anchors.L4: Reversible (mode changes / pull-back); refinement is signal-driven
anchors.L5: Compounding flywheel; trust/accuracy rise with use; scoped to agentic workflows

probing_questions.q: How mature is the team's flywheel — do usage signals (override rate, escalations, corrections) systematically drive refinement, or is improvement reactive/manual?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests flywheel maturity. Strong: systematic, signal-driven refinement. Weak: reactive, manual, or none.

probing_questions.q: Is reversibility an established discipline — does the team re-calibrate pairing modes or pull work back based on signals, as a norm?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests governance maturity. Strong: reversibility is practiced. Weak: one-way promotion, no recalibration.

probing_questions.q: Does the team track override rate (and similar health signals) as a standard metric for agentic steps?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the key-signal discipline. Strong: override rate tracked as standard. Weak: not tracked — blind to a failing skill.

probing_questions.q: Across its agentic workflows over time, how well can the team demonstrate compounding — trust and accuracy rising with use?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests demonstrable compounding. Strong: evidence of compounding. Weak: flat, no evidence.

nodes.label: 6.7 Human-AI Interaction & UX Design
nodes.summary: Adoption and safe use depend on the interface, not just model quality: users must see uncertainty, verify, correct, and escalate. Bad UX causes over-trust or abandonment regardless of model accuracy.

anchors.L1: Raw model output dumped to users; no failure/loading/empty states; no correction path
anchors.L2: Basic UI; some error handling; uncertainty/correction ad-hoc
anchors.L3: Failure/loading/empty states, escalation/correction paths, and uncertainty/citations designed as standard
anchors.L4: UX patterns reused across builds; trust calibrated (provenance, confidence); the creator->editor human boundary designed in
anchors.L5: Interaction quality measured (trust calibration, override/abandonment, in-UI task success) and continuously improved; UX is a managed asset

probing_questions.q: How does the team design the INTERFACE around the agentic step — failure, loading, and empty states; what the user sees when the model errs, a tool times out, or retrieval is empty — as a standard, or is raw model output dumped to the user?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests interaction maturity. Strong: failure/loading/empty states designed as a norm. Weak: raw output dumped; the UI breaks on the unhappy path.

probing_questions.q: How does the team communicate UNCERTAINTY and PROVENANCE (confidence, what's supported, citations/sources) so users can calibrate trust rather than over- or under-trust the agent?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests trust-calibration design. Strong: uncertainty + provenance surfaced so users verify appropriately. Weak: confident-looking output with no way to judge or check it.

probing_questions.q: Is the human's CORRECTION / OVERRIDE / ESCALATION path designed into the experience itself (not just a backend capability) — can the user easily challenge, fix, or escalate when the AI is wrong?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the human-boundary-in-the-UI (creator->editor). Strong: an obvious in-product correct/override/escalate path. Weak: the user can't easily contest a wrong answer.

probing_questions.q: Does the team MEASURE and improve interaction quality over time (trust calibration, override/abandonment rates, in-UI task success), or is UX a one-time build?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests UX-as-managed-asset. Strong: interaction metrics tracked and the UX iterated. Weak: shipped once, never measured.

nodes.label: Dimension 7: Workforce, Talent & Operating Model
nodes.summary: Assessment dimension 7 of the nine-dimension maturity model: Workforce, Talent & Operating Model. Contains 7 criteria scored L1-L5.

nodes.label: 7.1 AI Fluency & Role-Based Training (enterprise-wide)
nodes.summary: Talent readiness is the lowest AI-readiness dimension; enterprise-wide, role-appropriate enablement is foundational to the transformation.

anchors.L1: No structured AI training, or only a few technical people
anchors.L3: Role-based learning paths; agentic skills targeted; citizen-builder enablement
anchors.L4: Enterprise-wide enablement (every function/level) with role-appropriate depth; continuous reskilling
anchors.L5: Enterprise-wide, continuous, MEASURED capability uplift; AI fluency a baseline expectation for all

probing_questions.q: Is AI/agent fluency treated as table stakes ACROSS THE WHOLE ENTERPRISE (every function and level), with role-appropriate depth — or only for technical teams?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests breadth of enablement. Strong: enterprise-wide, role-appropriate enablement for everyone. Weak: training confined to technical/specialist teams → the rest of the org can't use/guide AI.

probing_questions.q: Are there role-differentiated learning paths (leaders, builders, citizen developers, end users), and does training target AGENTIC skills (orchestration, skill-building, supervising agents) rather than only classical data-science/ML?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests role-fit and agentic focus. Strong: differentiated paths targeting agentic skills. Weak: one generic course, or classical-ML training that misses the agentic shift.

probing_questions.q: Is there a continuous reskilling cadence as roles and tools change, plus enablement for citizen builders?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests sustainability. Strong: continuous reskilling + citizen-builder enablement. Weak: one-time training that goes stale.

probing_questions.q: How do you measure enablement reach and capability uplift (coverage, fluency, active builders) — not just course completions?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests outcome focus. Strong: measured reach + capability uplift. Weak: vanity metrics (completions) or no measurement.

nodes.label: 7.2 New Agentic-Era Roles & Role Consolidation
nodes.summary: Agentic roles exploded (~280% YoY); a full-stack person with skills does what used to need a team of specialists.

anchors.L3: New agentic roles + human-around-agent roles defined
anchors.L4: Deliberate consolidation into full-stack-with-skills; lifecycle/risk roles owned
anchors.L5: Role model fully reframed; generalists own value streams with fewer handoffs

probing_questions.q: Has the team defined the new agentic roles it needs (agentic AI engineer, agent architect, AI trainer, forward-deployed engineer, agent lifecycle owner, AI risk/governance)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests role definition. Strong: new roles defined and staffed. Weak: organizing around the pre-AI specialist catalog.

probing_questions.q: Are the human roles around the agent defined (input/grounding, reasoning/prompt design, quality standards, safety oversight)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the human-around-agent model. Strong: these responsibilities are clear and owned. Weak: undefined → quality/safety gaps.

probing_questions.q: Is role consolidation into full-stack-with-skills generalists deliberate (fewer handoffs, more value-stream owned per person)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the consolidation thesis. Strong: deliberate generalist consolidation. Weak: still many specialists with heavy handoffs.

probing_questions.q: Are job families/role definitions updated for the agentic era, or still the pre-AI catalog?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests role-catalog currency. Strong: updated job families. Weak: hiring/organizing to obsolete definitions.

nodes.label: 7.3 Team Structure & Composition
nodes.summary: Capability scales independently of headcount; the shift is two-pizza -> one-pizza / agent-augmented cells — absorbing MORE scope, not just cutting heads.

anchors.L3: Deliberate smaller agent-augmented cells
anchors.L4: Full-stack pods + agents; sized by leverage/scope; scope-increase acknowledged
anchors.L5: One-pizza/agent-augmented product cells the norm; capability scales independent of headcount

probing_questions.q: Is team topology deliberately designed as smaller, agent-augmented cells (humans + agents)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests topology intent. Strong: deliberate agent-augmented cells. Weak: large, handoff-heavy specialist teams; 'AI bolted on a bicycle'.

probing_questions.q: Does composition mix the needed roles (vision/PM, builder/architecture, quality/ops) + agents, with fewer handoffs?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests composition. Strong: right roles + agents, fewer handoffs. Weak: composition unchanged from pre-AI.

probing_questions.q: Do you account for smaller teams absorbing MORE scope (rising judgment demand), not just cutting headcount?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the caveat. Strong: leverage framing (more scope, more judgment). Weak: naive headcount cuts without the leverage to back them.

probing_questions.q: Is team sizing decided by leverage/scope, or by headcount-as-capacity?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the core reframe. Strong: sized by leverage. Weak: 'want 2x output, hire 2x people'.

nodes.label: 7.4 Hiring for the Agentic Era
nodes.summary: The scarce profile is the AI-fluent generalist with judgment; hiring the old specialist profile fills the team with the wrong capability.

anchors.L3: Hiring profile updated (fluency, generalist, judgment)
anchors.L4: Process screens for AI-leverage + judgment; strong brand/fast process; anchor hires
anchors.L5: Magnet for AI-fluent generalists; deliberate new-role hiring; productive in week one

probing_questions.q: Is the hiring profile updated for the agentic era (AI fluency, generalist/full-stack range, agentic-orchestration, judgment/taste, FDE-type hybrids)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the profile. Strong: hires AI-fluent generalists with judgment. Weak: hiring the old specialist profile.

probing_questions.q: Does the process screen for AI-leveraged capability and judgment, not just classical specialization?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the screen. Strong: screens for AI-leverage + judgment. Weak: classical credential/specialization screening only.

probing_questions.q: Has the org adapted to 'the candidate interviews you' (employer brand, fast process, anchor hires)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests hiring competitiveness. Strong: compelling brand, fast process, anchor hires. Weak: slow, generic process loses AI-fluent talent.

probing_questions.q: Do you hire the new agentic roles deliberately, or backfill old roles?
