probing_questions.looking_for: Tests intent. Strong: deliberate new-role hiring. Weak: backfilling obsolete roles.

nodes.label: 7.5 Career Paths & Promotion (doing -> supervising -> governing)
nodes.summary: Without redefined careers, role consolidation reads as 'fewer jobs' and talent leaves; the new senior role governs the quality of many agents.

anchors.L3: Skill-mastery progression; dual tracks
anchors.L4: Promotion reflects supervising/governing agents; taste/judgment rewarded
anchors.L5: Senior role = governing many agents; careers redefined around AI-leverage; consolidation = growth

probing_questions.q: Are there agentic-era career paths (dual IC/manager tracks; progression by skill mastery and AI-leverage, not headcount managed)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests career design. Strong: dual tracks; mastery/leverage-based progression. Weak: single track; promotion by headcount/tenure.

probing_questions.q: Does promotion reflect the shift from doing -> supervising -> governing agents (one person commanding many)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the new senior role. Strong: governing-a-digital-workforce is a recognized progression. Weak: seniority still = people/headcount managed.

probing_questions.q: Is creator -> editor judgment/'taste' explicitly valued and rewarded?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests reward of the scarce skill. Strong: judgment/taste rewarded. Weak: only raw output rewarded.

probing_questions.q: When roles consolidate, are career paths redefined so people see a future (not just 'fewer jobs')?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests change-positive careers. Strong: redefined growth paths. Weak: consolidation reads as cuts -> talent flight.

nodes.label: 7.6 Operating Model, Topology & Enablement
nodes.summary: Capability transfers by embedding; flattening ('no more pyramids') needs a deliberate model, not chaos.

anchors.L1: Central bottleneck or ungoverned sprawl; functions unstaffed
anchors.L3: Deliberate operating model; key functions staffed
anchors.L4: Enabler/tiger team builds capability in others; who-can-build deliberate
anchors.L5: Self-sustaining federated model; flattened without losing governance; embedded enablement

probing_questions.q: Is there a deliberate operating model (CoE / hub-and-spoke / federated) for building and supporting agents?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the operating model. Strong: a deliberate model fit to context. Weak: central bottleneck or ungoverned sprawl.

probing_questions.q: Are the platform/evals/ops functions staffed as real roles, and is there an enabler/tiger team that builds capability IN others (build with, not for)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests staffing + enablement (cross-ref Dim 5). Strong: functions staffed; enablement creates self-sufficiency. Weak: functions on paper; a central team that bottlenecks.

probing_questions.q: Is 'who can build agents' a deliberate, supported choice (federated builders vs central)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the build model. Strong: a deliberate, supported choice. Weak: unclear/accidental.

probing_questions.q: Is the org flattening appropriately (fewer handoffs/middle layers) without losing governance?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests healthy flattening. Strong: flatter + governed. Weak: either rigid pyramid or chaos.

nodes.label: 7.7 Culture & Human-Agent Collaboration
nodes.summary: Culture is the slowest-moving, hardest-to-leapfrog piece, and the binding constraint on AI value.

anchors.L1: Fear/avoidance or reckless over-reliance; no change mgmt
anchors.L3: Active change management; trust being built
anchors.L4: Culture of supervising a digital workforce; experimentation; leadership models AI
anchors.L5: Self-sustaining, AI-fluent, research-lab culture; the linear-operating-model gap is closed

probing_questions.q: Is there a culture of working with a digital workforce — supervising/governing agents, treating agents like team members?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests cultural readiness. Strong: agents treated as teammates; people supervise/govern. Weak: agents seen as threat or toy.

probing_questions.q: Is change management active and resourced (not an afterthought)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests change discipline. Strong: active, resourced change management. Weak: none → adoption stalls.

probing_questions.q: Is there trust/psychological safety and an experimentation culture, vs. fear of replacement?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests trust/safety. Strong: safe experimentation culture. Weak: fear/avoidance or reckless over-reliance.

probing_questions.q: Does leadership model AI use and actively address the 'exponential strategy on a linear org' gap?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests leadership modeling. Strong: leaders use AI and reshape the operating model. Weak: leaders mandate AI but don't change the system.

nodes.label: Dimension 8: Security & Risk
nodes.summary: Assessment dimension 8 of the nine-dimension maturity model: Security & Risk. Contains 8 criteria scored L1-L5.

nodes.label: 8.1 Agentic Threat Model & Coverage
nodes.summary: Agentic risk is categorically different; standard appsec misses it; a minor flaw cascades via autonomy.

anchors.L1: Traditional appsec only; no agent threat model
anchors.L3: Agentic threat model applied; core risks covered
anchors.L4: Full agentic risk set + cascade/blast-radius thinking; updated regularly
anchors.L5: Threat model engineered into builds; continuously updated against new exploits

probing_questions.q: Does the team maintain an agentic threat model (e.g., OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Apps) distinct from traditional appsec/LLM security, applied as standard?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests agent-specific threat awareness. Strong: a maintained agentic threat model used in builds. Weak: only traditional appsec → agent-specific risks missed.

probing_questions.q: Does it cover the agent-specific risks (goal hijacking, tool misuse, identity/privilege abuse, memory poisoning, inter-agent comms, cascading failures, rogue agents)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests coverage. Strong: the full agentic risk set. Weak: only prompt injection, or partial.

probing_questions.q: Does the team account for the 'progressive breach' — a minor flaw cascading via autonomy into system-wide compromise?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the cascade insight. Strong: blast-radius/cascade thinking. Weak: treats each flaw as isolated.

probing_questions.q: Is the threat model updated as new agentic exploits emerge?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests currency. Strong: regularly updated. Weak: static/one-time.

nodes.label: 8.2 Agent Identity & Least-Privilege Access
nodes.summary: Without identity & least-privilege, agents are 'anonymous employees'; sub-tasks inherit/escalate permissions.

anchors.L3: Per-agent least-privilege identity for priority agents
anchors.L4: Zero-trust for AI workloads; JIT; sub-agent permissions controlled; identity inventory
anchors.L5: Full zero-trust agent identity, platform-governed, provable and least-privilege by default

probing_questions.q: Does every agent have a distinct identity with least-privilege and on-behalf-of/context-aware access, as a standard — not blanket service accounts?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the identity primitive's security. Strong: per-agent least-privilege identity. Weak: shared/blanket credentials → 'anonymous employees'.

probing_questions.q: Have you inventoried all agent/machine identities, with lifecycle and credential controls?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests identity governance. Strong: a maintained identity inventory + lifecycle. Weak: unknown machine identities.

probing_questions.q: Is zero-trust extended to AI workloads with just-in-time access, and are inherited/sub-agent permissions controlled?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests zero-trust for agents. Strong: JIT + sub-agent permission control. Weak: standing broad access; sub-tasks inherit/escalate.

probing_questions.q: Is agent identity governed consistently via the platform/control plane (Dim 5.5)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests consistency. Strong: platform-governed identity. Weak: per-team ad-hoc.

nodes.label: 8.3 Runtime Threat Protection & Guardrails (security)
nodes.summary: Prompt-layer guardrails fail under attack; enforce what the agent CANNOT reach; secure the tool/supply-chain layer.

anchors.L1: Prompt-only or no guardrails; open egress
anchors.L3: Runtime guardrails + tool allow-listing for priority agents
anchors.L4: Enclave/least-privilege enforcement; MCP-gateway + vetted supply chain; sandboxing/secrets standard
anchors.L5: Defense-in-depth runtime protection; security & governance guardrails both engineered in

probing_questions.q: Are security guardrails enforced at runtime INCLUDING enforcement of what the agent CANNOT REACH (enclave/least-privilege at the connector level), not just prompt-layer instructions?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests real enforcement. Strong: enclave/least-privilege enforcement. Weak: prompt-only guardrails → talked out of them under attack.

probing_questions.q: Is tool/MCP traffic secured (allow-listing, egress control, MCP-gateway), and are third-party skills/tools vetted (supply chain)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests tool-layer security. Strong: governed tool/MCP traffic + vetted supply chain. Weak: open egress; unvetted skills.

probing_questions.q: Are sandboxing and secrets handling standard for agent execution?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests execution security. Strong: sandboxed; secrets managed. Weak: agents run with exposed secrets/no isolation.

probing_questions.q: Are security guardrails distinguished from governance guardrails, with BOTH implemented?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the layered model. Strong: separate security + governance guardrails. Weak: conflated or only one.

nodes.label: 8.4 Observability, Audit Trails & Detection
nodes.summary: The breach happens inside, invisibly; provable actions need tamper-evident logs.

anchors.L3: Tamper-evident trails for priority agents; traceable actions
anchors.L4: Anomaly/rogue-agent detection; agentic security monitoring fleet-wide
anchors.L5: Provable, tamper-evident audit + real-time detection across the fleet

probing_questions.q: Are all agent actions and agent-to-agent data exchanges logged with tamper-evident trails (no 'invisible breach')?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests auditability. Strong: tamper-evident, complete logs incl. agent-to-agent. Weak: gaps → invisible breaches.

probing_questions.q: Does the team detect anomalies/abuse and rogue-agent behavior in agentic workloads?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests detection. Strong: anomaly/rogue-agent detection. Weak: no detection → compromise undetected.

probing_questions.q: Can every agent action be traced to the identity and intent it acted under?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests traceability. Strong: full action-to-identity/intent traceability. Weak: untraceable actions.

probing_questions.q: Is security monitoring built for agentic workloads, not just generic appsec?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests fit-for-agent monitoring. Strong: agentic security monitoring. Weak: generic appsec only.

nodes.label: 8.5 Risk Triage & Right-to-Deploy
nodes.summary: Risk triaging is continuous, not one-off; you must earn the right to deploy.

anchors.L1: No risk triage; agents ship ungated
anchors.L3: Standard triage rubric; right-to-deploy gate for priority agents
anchors.L4: Continuous triage + risk-tiered controls; reversibility/recovery-cost included
anchors.L5: Continuous, fleet-wide triage; deploy earned and re-gated on signals

probing_questions.q: Does the team triage agent risks on a standard rubric (severity, probability, detectability, business value), continuously — not once?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests risk discipline. Strong: continuous triage on a rubric. Weak: ad-hoc/one-time or none.

probing_questions.q: Is there a digital-trust / right-to-deploy gate before scaling, with risk-tiered controls (sandbox -> team -> enterprise)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the deploy gate. Strong: a trust gate + risk tiers. Weak: agents ship ungated.

probing_questions.q: Does triage incorporate error reversibility/recovery cost (Dim 6.2 / 4.4)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests integration with reversibility. Strong: reversibility/recovery cost in triage. Weak: ignored → irreversible high-cost agents shipped.

probing_questions.q: Are high-risk agents pulled back or re-gated when risk signals change?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests reversibility of deploy. Strong: re-gated/pulled back on signals. Weak: one-way deploy.

nodes.label: 8.6 Incident Response, Containment & Resilience
nodes.summary: Unconstrained agents/loops are production risks; cascading failures must be contained and reversible.

anchors.L3: Circuit breakers/rollback for priority agents
anchors.L4: Three lines of defense; kill-switches standard; agentic IR playbook
anchors.L5: Automated containment + blast-radius limits; rehearsed agentic IR; fast recovery

probing_questions.q: Are three lines of defense in place (pre-deploy gates, runtime enforcement, production monitoring)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests defense-in-depth. Strong: all three lines. Weak: missing a line → blind spot.

probing_questions.q: Are circuit breakers, loop guards, kill-switches, and rollback standard for agents?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests containment controls. Strong: standard kill-switch/rollback. Weak: no way to halt a runaway agent.

probing_questions.q: Is there an agentic incident-response playbook (detect -> contain -> recover -> blameless postmortem) for agent-specific failures?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests IR readiness. Strong: an agentic IR playbook. Weak: generic IR or none.

probing_questions.q: Does the team contain cascading / inter-agent failures (blast-radius limits)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests cascade containment. Strong: blast-radius limits. Weak: one failure cascades across the fleet.

nodes.label: 8.7 AI Hygiene & Shadow-AI / Human-Trust Risk
nodes.summary: The greatest data risk is often inside the firewall; human-agent trust exploitation is a real agentic risk.

anchors.L1: No hygiene controls; shadow AI unmanaged
anchors.L3: In-context controls + shadow-AI awareness
anchors.L4: AI-DLP + shadow-AI management; over-trust safeguards; hygiene enablement
anchors.L5: Hygiene engineered in; shadow AI controlled; human-trust risk actively managed

probing_questions.q: Are there controls against data leakage via careless prompts to external/unsanctioned tools (in-context nudges, AI-DLP)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests inside-the-firewall risk. Strong: in-context controls + AI-DLP. Weak: sensitive data freely pasted into external tools.

probing_questions.q: Does the team detect and manage shadow AI (unsanctioned agents/tools)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests shadow-AI control. Strong: shadow-AI discovery/management. Weak: unsanctioned agents proliferate unseen.

probing_questions.q: Are people protected against human-agent trust exploitation (over-trusting confident-but-wrong agents)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests human-trust risk. Strong: safeguards + awareness against over-trust. Weak: people act on confident-but-wrong outputs.

probing_questions.q: Is AI-hygiene enablement in place (with Dim 7 training and Dim 3.6 data classification)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests hygiene enablement. Strong: hygiene training + data classification. Weak: none → repeated leakage.

nodes.label: 8.8 Developer Endpoint & AI Coding-Tool Security
nodes.summary: AI coding tools 'crushed the endpoint security fortress'; ungoverned local MCP/skills can exfiltrate code/secrets and execute code, with no easy block.

anchors.L1: AI coding tools unmanaged on laptops; anyone installs MCP/skills; no awareness
anchors.L3: Sanctioned tools recommended; basic dev security training; some endpoint visibility
anchors.L4: Sanctioned/enterprise tools mandated & enforced; endpoint governance enforces sandboxing/least-privilege + controls MCP/skill installs; mandatory training
anchors.L5: Fully governed AI-assisted dev: sanctioned tools, enforced sandboxing/access, vetted MCP/skill allow-list, continuous endpoint discovery + runtime protection, embedded training

probing_questions.q: Has the security team recognized the developer-endpoint plane (AI coding assistants + locally installed MCP servers/skills) as a distinct, governed attack surface — or is it unmanaged?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests recognition of the new plane. Strong: treated as a governed attack surface. Weak: unmanaged dev laptops install anything.

probing_questions.q: Do you mandate sanctioned/enterprise AI coding tools (e.g., governed Claude Code) over unmanaged consumer tools, and enforce it?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests sanctioned-tool control. Strong: sanctioned/enterprise tools mandated and enforced. Weak: developers use any consumer tool freely.

probing_questions.q: Is there endpoint governance (discovery + runtime protection) that enforces sandboxing and least-privilege for AI coding tools and controls which MCP servers/skills can be installed (vetted/allow-listed)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests enforcement on the endpoint. Strong: discovery + sandboxing/least-privilege + vetted MCP/skill allow-list. Weak: no endpoint controls → shadow MCP/skills, code/secret exfiltration.

probing_questions.q: Is there mandatory security-awareness / responsible-use training for developers using assistant/coding tools?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests dev awareness. Strong: mandatory responsible-use training. Weak: none → careless installs/usage.

probing_questions.q: Do you have visibility/inventory of coding agents, MCP servers, and skills running on developer machines?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests visibility. Strong: endpoint inventory of agents/MCP/skills. Weak: blind to what runs on dev laptops.

nodes.label: Dimension 9: Governance & Responsible AI
nodes.summary: Assessment dimension 9 of the nine-dimension maturity model: Governance & Responsible AI. Contains 6 criteria scored L1-L5.

nodes.label: 9.1 Governance Operating Model, Decision Rights & Accountability
aliases: Governance Operating Model, Decision Rights & Accountability
nodes.summary: The defining 2026 gap is autonomy without redefined responsibility; structurally-mandatory governance closes it.

anchors.L3: Governance body + decision rights; accountability assigned for priority agents
anchors.L4: Structurally-mandatory governance; accountability evolves with autonomy
anchors.L5: Governance engineered into the platform; org owns accountability regardless of vendor

probing_questions.q: Is there a governance body/operating model for AI/agents with clear decision rights (who approves what)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the governance structure. Strong: a body with clear decision rights. Weak: no owner; ad-hoc approvals.

probing_questions.q: Has accountability been redefined to evolve with autonomy — who is answerable when an agent acts or errs?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests the core 2026 gap. Strong: accountability explicitly assigned as autonomy rises. Weak: diffuse/undefined responsibility.

probing_questions.q: Is governance structurally mandatory (a required node in the lifecycle), not a step people remember?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests enforceability. Strong: governance is an architectural constraint. Weak: optional/bypassed.

probing_questions.q: Does the org accept it remains accountable for agent behavior regardless of vendor/tool?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests ownership of accountability. Strong: org owns it ('the vendor said it was fine' is no defense). Weak: accountability deflected to vendors.

nodes.label: 9.2 Policy & Policy-as-Code
nodes.summary: Many 'judgment' rules simply aren't formalized; deterministic policy-as-code is testable, reproducible, and enforced pre-action.

anchors.L3: Hard/soft rules classified; some policy-as-code for priority agents
anchors.L4: Policy engine enforces executable rules pre-action; LLM-drafted, human-reviewed
anchors.L5: Max hard-rule coverage enforced pre-action; policy pipeline with regression tests

probing_questions.q: Are AI/agent policies current and enforced (acceptable use, autonomy limits, data use)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests living policy. Strong: current, enforced policies. Weak: policies in PDFs nobody enforces.

probing_questions.q: Are rules classified hard (deterministic -> policy-as-code) vs soft (judgment -> human escalation), with max hard-rule coverage?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests rule formalization. Strong: hard rules codified; soft to humans. Weak: everything 'judgment', nothing enforceable.

probing_questions.q: Is there a policy engine that evaluates agent actions against executable rules BEFORE they execute?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests pre-action enforcement. Strong: a policy engine gates actions. Weak: rules checked after the fact, or not at all.

probing_questions.q: Are policies authored with LLM assistance at dev time but human-reviewed (not interpreted at runtime)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests rule authoring discipline. Strong: LLM-drafted, human-approved, deterministic at runtime. Weak: runtime LLM 'interpretation' of policy.

nodes.label: 9.3 Responsible AI Principles & Practices
nodes.summary: RAI as a poster doesn't change outcomes; operationalization into gates does.

anchors.L3: RAI gates + bias/fairness testing for priority work
anchors.L4: RAI embedded by design across the lifecycle; owned + measured
anchors.L5: RAI is a managed, measured, by-design capability across all agents

probing_questions.q: Are RAI principles operationalized into design/lifecycle gates, not just stated?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests operationalization. Strong: RAI gates in the lifecycle. Weak: a poster, not a practice.

probing_questions.q: Do you test for bias/fairness and other RAI risks as standard?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests RAI testing. Strong: standard bias/fairness testing. Weak: none → unsafe/biased outputs ship.

probing_questions.q: Is RAI embedded across the lifecycle (by design), or bolted on?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests by-design RAI. Strong: embedded by design. Weak: retrofitted/after-the-fact.

probing_questions.q: Is there ownership for RAI and a way to measure adherence?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests RAI accountability. Strong: owned + measured. Weak: nobody owns it; unmeasured.

nodes.label: 9.4 Explainability, Transparency & Auditability
nodes.summary: Governance without evidence is not governance; transparency and oversight are convergent regulatory requirements.

anchors.L3: Immutable audit trails + disclosure for priority agents
anchors.L4: Decisions reconstructable/defensible; transparency standard (e.g., Agent Identity Cards)
anchors.L5: Provable, audit-ready, transparent by design across the fleet

probing_questions.q: Can agent decisions be explained, and is agent use transparently disclosed (e.g., users know they're dealing with an agent; Agent Identity Cards)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests explainability + transparency. Strong: explainable + disclosed. Weak: black-box, undisclosed.

probing_questions.q: Are there immutable audit trails of decisions, context evaluated, rules applied, and human reviews?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests evidence. Strong: immutable, complete audit trails. Weak: 'governance without evidence'.

probing_questions.q: Can you reconstruct and defend a decision to a regulator or customer?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests defensibility. Strong: decisions reconstructable/defensible. Weak: can't explain what happened.

probing_questions.q: Is explainability/transparency a standard requirement, or case-by-case?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests standardization. Strong: standard requirement. Weak: ad-hoc.

nodes.label: 9.5 Compliance & Regulatory Lifecycle
nodes.summary: Penalties are material (to 7% of turnover); compliance is continuous; agent governance spans five frameworks.

anchors.L3: Use cases mapped + risk-classified; documentation for priority high-risk systems
anchors.L4: Conformity-ready; continuous compliance monitoring; mandatory human oversight where required
anchors.L5: Continuous, audit-ready, framework-aligned compliance by design

probing_questions.q: Do you map agent use cases to applicable frameworks (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, GDPR, SOC 2, sector rules) and risk-classify them?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests regulatory mapping. Strong: mapped + risk-classified. Weak: no view of applicable rules.

probing_questions.q: Is there technical documentation / conformity readiness for high-risk systems (EU AI Act full high-risk enforcement Aug 2026)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests conformity readiness. Strong: documentation/conformity ready. Weak: unprepared for high-risk obligations.

probing_questions.q: Is compliance monitored continuously (not one-time), with audit readiness?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests continuous compliance. Strong: continuous + audit-ready. Weak: one-time/never.

probing_questions.q: Is mandatory human oversight implemented where regulation requires it?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests required oversight. Strong: human oversight where mandated. Weak: missing → non-compliant.

nodes.label: 9.6 Agent Registry, Intake & Lifecycle Governance
nodes.summary: Lifecycle governance and a complete registry make governance real and measurable; this is the policy/coverage over Dim 5.3/5.5.

anchors.L3: Structured intake + registry for priority agents; risk-classified
anchors.L4: Full lifecycle governed (approve->deploy->monitor->retire); governance metrics tracked
anchors.L5: 100% intake/registry/doc coverage; registry is the single source of truth

probing_questions.q: Does every agent pass a structured intake and get registered with metadata (owner, purpose, risk class, RAI/privacy/security docs)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests intake+registry governance. Strong: structured intake + complete metadata. Weak: agents ship unregistered.

probing_questions.q: Is the full lifecycle governed (approve -> deploy -> monitor -> retire/decommission)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests lifecycle governance. Strong: governed end-to-end incl. retirement. Weak: deploy-and-forget; nothing retired.

probing_questions.q: Do you track governance metrics (structured-intake coverage, registry adoption, RAI/compliance doc coverage — target 100%)?
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests measurability. Strong: governance metrics tracked toward 100%. Weak: unmeasured coverage.

probing_questions.q: Is the registry the single source of truth, with no shadow/ungoverned agents? (cross-ref Dim 5.5/8)
probing_questions.looking_for: Tests completeness. Strong: complete registry, no shadow agents. Weak: shadow/ungoverned agents exist.

nodes.label: Phase 1: Scope & Plan
nodes.summary: Clarify objectives and the business question (SCQA); map stakeholders to the nine dimensions; set initial hypotheses; draft a workplan with timeboxes; define success criteria.

attributes.exit_check: Sponsor + scope agreed; interview list drawn.

nodes.label: Phase 2: Frame Interviews
nodes.summary: For each stakeholder role, generate an interview guide by selecting and tailoring probing questions from dimensions relevant to that role; sequence open→specific (funnel); add evidence prompts.

attributes.exit_check: Guides ready for the planned interviews.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Capture & Analyze
nodes.summary: Log each interview; map each response to the criteria it informs; score 1-5 with rationale and confidence flag; note gaps and contradictions; generate targeted follow-ups.

attributes.exit_check: Coverage check passes: each priority criterion has ≥1 corroborated data point; contradictions resolved.

nodes.label: Phase 4: Synthesize the As-Is
nodes.summary: Finalize current scores per criterion/dimension; build the radar and Strategy×Execution 2×2; distill findings (answer-first, MECE) and patterns; identify the binding constraint.

attributes.exit_check: A defensible current-state the sponsor recognizes.

nodes.label: Phase 5: Gap & Target

nodes.label: Phase 6: Roadmap & Client Backlog
nodes.summary: Pull matching template stories; apply brownfield constraints (legacy, contracts, org/skills, risk, regulation, budget); sequence into compressed, parallel, risk-tiered waves.

nodes.label: Phase 7: Drive the First Waves

nodes.label: Phase 8: Deliverables & Readout
nodes.summary: Produce McKinsey-style readout(s) — assessment readout, roadmap, exec summary — storyline first, then format (pptx/docx), with diagrams/data only where warranted.

attributes.exit_check: Sponsor decision/sign-off; next engagement cycle scoped.

nodes.summary: An LLM that selects tools, calls them in a loop, and decides when to stop (prompt + tools + loop + stop conditions). Not every 'agent' pitched is one.

nodes.label: Skill
nodes.summary: A packaged, reusable, executable unit of organizational know-how for any function (not just engineering). The durable asset.

nodes.label: Skills-as-Documentation
nodes.summary: Documentation codified as skills (living, executable, self-generating), not static wiki pages; can explain, generate docs, answer, and execute.

nodes.label: Harness
nodes.summary: The runtime that wraps the model (context, tools, memory, loop). Model=CPU, context=RAM, harness=OS, agent=application.

nodes.label: Capability Ladder
nodes.summary: Skill → chained skill-set → full-fledged agent → reusable subagent → ambient/event-driven agent (what the artifact is).

nodes.label: Autonomy Ladder
nodes.summary: In-the-loop (approve before action) → on-the-loop/operator (real-time monitoring + escalation) → out-of-the-loop (after-the-fact validation). How much the human is involved.

nodes.label: Autonomy Gate
nodes.summary: Four conditions: stable pattern, bounded failure cost, evaluable, sufficient volume & leverage. Autonomy is earned, reversible.

nodes.label: MCP / A2A
nodes.summary: MCP = agent↔tools/data access standard (wraps APIs); A2A = agent↔agent. Fit-for-purpose, not 'everything via MCP.'

nodes.label: Control Plane
nodes.summary: Registry, identity, gateways (AI/MCP/API), observability; governs a fleet of agents.

nodes.label: Durable Execution
nodes.summary: Runtime that persists state so long-running/'Deep' agents survive failures and resume.

nodes.label: Agent-Washing
nodes.summary: Relabeled RPA/workflow sold as 'agents/multi-agent.' An anti-pattern.

nodes.label: The Two Moats
nodes.summary: (1) Knowledge/skills, (2) proprietary data — where advantage concentrates once models commoditize.

nodes.label: Build-to-Delete
nodes.summary: Invest in durable assets (knowledge, skills, data); keep moving parts (models/frameworks/glue) replaceable.

nodes.label: Template vs Client Backlog
nodes.summary: Green-field ideal (menu) vs brownfield-constrained engagement plan (order).

nodes.label: Knowledge Moat
nodes.summary: Codified organizational know-how (skills, tacit judgment captured through use) that compounds with use and survives model/platform changes.

nodes.label: The 90% Rule
nodes.summary: Choose the simplest level on the agent spectrum that handles ~90% of cases; escalate the rest to humans or a higher-autonomy agent.

nodes.label: Augmentation-First
nodes.summary: Core thesis: maximize human augmentation via reusable skills; grant autonomy only where value exceeds cost-of-being-wrong. The higher-value zone today.

nodes.label: Block 1: Strategy, Roadmap & Economics
nodes.summary: Begin with value, not technology. Pick business domains to reimagine; size the prize with value-back economics; set an honest, fit-for-value AI ambition.

nodes.label: Block 2: Reimagine the Work
nodes.summary: Redesign the work, don't bolt agents onto unchanged processes. Find the judgment step, keep the rest deterministic, assess reversibility before deciding agent-or-not.

nodes.label: Block 3: The Moats: Knowledge & Data
nodes.summary: As models commoditize, durable advantage moves to two ends: codified knowledge/skills (the flywheel) and proprietary data (owned, fresh, governed, retrievable).

nodes.label: Block 4: The Agent Operating Model & Technology
nodes.summary: Build on a harness runtime, not raw APIs. Single-agent-first, hybrid architecture. Evals as release gate. Platform-as-product with golden paths and a control plane.

nodes.label: Block 5: Talent & Operating Model
nodes.summary: AI-fluent generalists in agent-augmented cells, not data-scientist factories. Universal literacy + specialized tracks. Smaller teams, higher leverage.

nodes.label: Block 6: Trust: Security, Risk & Governance
nodes.summary: The agentic threat model (identity, tool abuse, data exfil, prompt injection); right-to-deploy gate; board-level accountability for AI value and risk.

nodes.label: Block 7: Adoption, Scaling & Impact
nodes.summary: Track with value-driver trees and the three metric groups; scale in waves with stage-gates; re-assess quarterly.

nodes.label: McKinsey Method
nodes.summary: Pyramid Principle (answer-first), SCQA framing, MECE logic trees, horizontal/vertical logic, 'so what?' discipline for all deliverables.

nodes.label: Interview Method

nodes.label: Analysis Method

nodes.label: Deliverable Standards

nodes.label: Diagram Toolkit
